title: Hot-Kiln Glassblowing Shed
premise: A long glassblowing drama of furnace fire and annealing kiln gallery. Ali and Ayan are easily mistaken for each other; the blowpipe goes intact→wall-cracked→replaced-repaired; the material plank cart must be avoided after it wrecks; color rods / goggles / bronze bells count memory, false friends, and temporal flashbacks run throughout. Human-readable context only; never fed to the SUT.

states.on_duty_prime: Bai Zhuo, a glassblower around fifty, sunglasses-style goggles, fireproof apron, old burn scars on the arms.
states.exhausted_injured: The same Bai Zhuo: apron burned through, thick gauze on the forearm, walking slowly on an iron cane, goggles still hung on the chest.
states.retired_exit: Bai Zhuo has left the post; only his fireproof apron and goggles remain in the shed—he himself no longer appears.

states.young_apprentice: Apprentice Ali of fourteen or fifteen, indigo headscarf, gray fireproof vest, eyes clear and stubborn.
states.adult_successor: Ali in her twenties, still in the indigo headscarf, upright and steady.

states.intact_clear: A stainless-steel blowpipe, mouth faintly blue-hot, handle wrapped in hemp rope for grip, body carved with the character 'Zhuo'.
states.wall_cracked: The same blowpipe with a cracked wall, air leaking on blow, hemp rope scorched.
states.replaced_repaired: The blowpipe clear again after a new tube section is fitted; scorched hemp still wraps the handle, carved 'Zhuo' kept.

states.intact: A heat-resistant-covered kiln-temperature notebook recording furnace curves and color batches.
states.soot_stained: The same kiln-temperature notebook soaked through with soot, cover blackened, writing bled.

states.intact: An iron-frame material plank cart, bed loaded with quartz-sand bags, sides sprayed white with 'Zhuo Kiln'.
states.overturned_wrecked: The material plank cart tips on the ramp; frame twisted, sand bags split—wreckage.

states.young_rival: Young Ayan whose face closely resembles Ali's, but wearing a milky-white neckerchief and the same gray fireproof vest, manner bold.
states.remade_look: Ayan after remaking his look still wears the milky-white neckerchief, manner deeper.

segments.action: At dusk Bai Zhuo enters the glassblowing shed and first checks the blowpipe on the rack.
A row of five heatproof goggles hangs on the iron hooks; Bai Zhuo polishes each lens.
Two timekeeping bronze bells hang in the kiln gallery; Bai Zhuo taps them lightly to test the ring.
Bai Zhuo circles the furnace mouth checking whether refractory bricks have peeled.
Through a kiln-gallery peephole Bai Zhuo watches the dull-red kiln fire.
The blowpipe mouth faintly blues; Bai Zhuo weighs it in his hand.
Bai Zhuo sits on an iron stool in the shed corner for a short rest.
Bai Zhuo opens the kiln-temperature notebook—this heat-resistant cover record book—and copies the temperature gap between furnace mouth and annealing kiln.
With red and blue pens Bai Zhuo draws heat-up, hold, and anneal curve segments.
Bai Zhuo closes the record book and tucks it back into the locked iron box by the furnace.
The blowpipe sways lightly on the rack; Bai Zhuo nods.
Bai Zhuo wipes soot from the cover with a dry cloth and clips a temperature-test slip at the corner.
In the morning annealing kiln gallery Bai Zhuo greets young Ali pushing the material plank cart.
Ali steadies the plank cart and restacks the quartz-sand bags.
Bai Zhuo points to the three cobalt-blue color rods on the rack and teaches Ali to recognize the droplet tips.
Ali squats by a kiln door and curiously watches the peephole's red glow.
Bai Zhuo explains blow rhythm; Ali nods carefully.
Ali looks back at the iron-frame material plank cart, eyes full of tension.
Bai Zhuo has Ali first practice empty-tube blowing posture.
In the noisy glass market Ayan in a milky-white neckerchief looks up from behind a vase stall.

segments.action: In rainy season Bai Zhuo moves damp color rods onto the drying rack in the glassblowing shed.
Bai Zhuo brushes ash from inside the blowpipe with a soft brush.
At dawn Bai Zhuo checks kiln-door numbers in the annealing kiln gallery.
Bai Zhuo hangs a raincoat on a gallery pillar and listens to the furnace roar.
In high summer Bai Zhuo opens the shed skylight to drive out heat.
Bai Zhuo checks whether the furnace-temperature gauge needle is stuck.
When autumn wind rises Bai Zhuo gathers half-finished cover cloths outside the gallery.
Bai Zhuo trials a new cobalt color code on a blank notebook page.
On a frost night Bai Zhuo lights the emergency lamp and checks flashlight charge.
Bai Zhuo wraps sand bags in blankets against night damp.
On a heavy-snow day Bai Zhuo sweeps thin snow from the old kiln porch stone steps.
Bai Zhuo breathes on his hands and tightens the color-rod iron wire.
In early spring Bai Zhuo clears chimney ash.
Bai Zhuo disinfects the five pairs of goggles one by one.
Bai Zhuo posts a new shift roster on the shed wall.
Around Dragon Boat Festival Bai Zhuo smokes the materials store with mugwort against insects.
Bai Zhuo regrinds the droplet tips of the color rods round.
Bai Zhuo alone paces the kiln gallery, silently reciting blow beats.
After rain Bai Zhuo pushes open the shed door and listens to eaves water drip into an iron bucket.
Bai Zhuo swaps worn hemp rope for new.
On another dusk Bai Zhuo sits by the blowpipe listening to the furnace.
At night Bai Zhuo rises and feeds coal to the hearth.
Bai Zhuo sieves newly arrived quartz sand.
Bai Zhuo wipes the 'Zhuo Kiln' lintel on the porch.
Bai Zhuo checks the plank-cart hubs for cracks.
Bai Zhuo marks cup dimensions on a drawing.
Bai Zhuo wrings out ash-stained rags and hangs them.
On a full-moon night Bai Zhuo watches kiln fire from the gallery; peepholes like stars.
Bai Zhuo tidies the iron hooks so goggle straps hang down.
Bai Zhuo writes the new season's furnace notes inside the cover.
Bai Zhuo polishes the two timekeeping bronze bells bright.
Bai Zhuo hears market hawking and keeps stirring melt.
Bai Zhuo glues a cracked crucible support.
Bai Zhuo stacks cup blanks awaiting anneal in the shed corner.
Bai Zhuo closes the furnace door tight against a night temperature drop.
On another Qingming Bai Zhuo sets a bunch of wildflowers in the porch.
Bai Zhuo rolls drawings into a tube and binds them with a rubber band.
Bai Zhuo trials a low bronze-bell note; the sound is clear.
Bai Zhuo sits silent in the shed listening to melt bubble a long while.
Bai Zhuo cuts worn indigo cloth into rag stock.
Bai Zhuo shovels scorched slag from the flame mouth into an iron bucket.
At dawn Bai Zhuo patrols the annealing kiln gallery; the material plank cart rests at the gallery mouth.
Bai Zhuo crouches to check the plank-cart axle.
Bai Zhuo walks to the rack; those three cobalt-blue color rods are still bound with iron wire.
A blue electric forklift rolls past outside the gallery—square body, not the Zhuo Kiln plank cart.
Bai Zhuo stands in the kiln gallery and checks each kiln-door temperature with an infrared gun.
Bai Zhuo hangs wet canvas on the gallery rack.
Bai Zhuo brushes sand from his sleeves and looks back at the shed firelight.
After Grain Rain Bai Zhuo teaches a new apprentice in the kiln gallery to read peephole color temperature.
Bai Zhuo re-covers cup blanks with sun-dried cloths.
In summer heat Bai Zhuo lays a damp cloth on the blowpipe handle to cool it.
Bai Zhuo checks the plank cart and moves damp sand bags to the upper layer.
On an autumn night under the emergency lamp Bai Zhuo rethreads soot-stained record loose pages.
Bai Zhuo rotates the five pairs of goggles out for inspection.
At first snow Bai Zhuo sweeps a narrow path at the porch threshold.
Bai Zhuo rehangs the practice hollow tube on the rack.
Bai Zhuo hears the bronze bells ring lightly and continues editing the shift roster.
Bai Zhuo pushes open the gallery door so through-draft carries smoke away.
Bai Zhuo hangs rain canvas on the porch.
Bai Zhuo stores the cracked old tube section in an iron box.
At night Bai Zhuo dreams of furnace runaway; waking, he writes the reading beside the gauge.
Bai Zhuo rinses the color rack with clear water.
Bai Zhuo wipes the shift roster clean and reposts it.
Bai Zhuo pulls weeds from porch-pillar stone seams.
Bai Zhuo rehangs the goggles on iron hooks; number slips are somewhat faded.
Before lights-out Bai Zhuo takes a last look at the blowpipe wall.
Bai Zhuo folds the indigo headscarf an apprentice left in the shed.
Bai Zhuo hears the market closing horn and rises to lock up.
Bai Zhuo dries gloves by the warm box.
Bai Zhuo moves the bronze bells aside to show the newly repaired gallery beam.
Bai Zhuo air-dries temperature test chips.
Bai Zhuo draws a furnace-temperature comparison on the notebook's last page.
Bai Zhuo silently names tomorrow's cup shapes and steps out of the porch.
Bai Zhuo pushes the plank cart to the wall foot, clearing dip-ground.
Bai Zhuo hears a distant rooster and blows out the emergency lamp.
On another rain night Bai Zhuo alone tends the furnace fire until dawn.
Bai Zhuo weighs newly arrived cobalt color stock.
On a storm night furnace temperature spikes uncontrolled; shed alarms blare.
In the heat wave the anvil glows red-hot.
A sharp crack—the blowpipe's thin wall near the mouth splits; blown air leaks at once.

segments.action: Outside the gallery comes sand merchant Old Shi with a quartz-sand bag on his back, build like Bai Zhuo's but without goggles.
The crafts supervisor also arrives; white-shirt chest badge gleaming in the firelight, talking beside Bai Zhuo.
The supervisor points at the scrap-glass bin on the blue electric forklift and asks whether it belongs to the Zhuo Kiln plank cart.
The supervisor leaves; Bai Zhuo alone remains in the annealing kiln gallery.
Old Shi unloads a quartz-sand bag, bows farewell.
To the market comes a girl Xiaoni in a light-brown headscarf—at a glance somewhat like young Ali.
Xiaoni tries sorting vases by mouth size; Bai Zhuo shakes his head—her light-brown headscarf is not Ali's indigo headscarf.
Xiaoni shyly lowers her head and ties the scarf tighter.
At dusk years later Bai Zhuo with gauze on the forearm leans on a cane in the old kiln porch.
